Today, Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now, three hundred and fifty thousand people were watching her livestream, and the number was climbing rapidly as the broadcast moved into the Q&A segment.

If the live viewership hit four hundred thousand, it would be an absolute world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one before her had ever pulled it off. Even the famous and obscenely wealthy Tony Bobbins, in his heyday, had only drawn three hundred and ninety thousand—and that was after decades in the game and with a face recognized all over the world! Now Freya had a shot at shattering that ceiling with room to spare and securing her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought it was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune only smiles on prepared minds and hands ready to act.

At first, things had gone only decently. An hour went to a lecture on how to achieve your goals. It was the most enjoyable part, yet only a hundred thousand showed up. Expected, sure, but beneath Freya's level, with her four million on Instagram and another twelve on TikTok. She didn't care for the latter—too few serious people—but the algorithms had decided otherwise.

Another hour went to questions along the lines of "the best age to launch a startup" and "how to get up and get going," submitted by followers via a form before the stream. The questions landed well and pulled the live count up to two hundred thousand.

Still, it wasn't enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand—a plateau that was getting harder to break through every single time.

That was when Freya went all in, as the New York wheeler-dealers liked to say. In twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants slapped together a payment form and blasted out social media posts. And the surprise segment of the broadcast began: open questions in exchange for donations. Unmoderated, but on Freya's terms.
